samples.question: This image shows one button lying on white paper. The button is the large solid coloured disc. The grey page frame and the four short grey ticks near the corners are fixed decoration: they are drawn the same way in every image of this set and never indicate the answer. An OPENING is a hole cut right through the button: it appears as a white gap inside the disc, the same white as the paper around the button. The thin darker circle drawn near the rim of the button is painted decoration, not an opening. Any small solid coloured spots printed on the button are ink, not openings, because the paper does not show through them; they lie outside the ring of openings and must not be counted. The number of openings is always two, three, four, five or six, and it changes from image to image, as do their size and placement, the button's colour and size, and how many coloured spots are printed on it. Count the white openings you can actually see in this image, and do not answer from the number of holes a button usually has. How many openings does the button have? Answer with a single digit from 2 to 6.
